Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. After 26 years, the U.S. has lost
its measles-free status. According to the Pan American Health Organization, the announcement
comes as the country is reporting more than 5,400 cases with 10 associated deaths, and
PR's Maria Godoy has more. The determination means that measles is once again spreading
regularly in the U.S. Measles is incredibly contagious. High vaccination rates of at least
95 percent are needed to stop its spread. Since the pandemic, childhood vaccination rates have
fallen below that threshold, allowing outbreaks to take hold. In the coming weeks, the U.S.
is expected to submit a plan to the organization on how it plans to once again get measles under
control. Dr. Rhonda Seeley-Thomas with the Pan American Group says that would require
increasing vaccination rates, improving surveillance, and having a rapid response plan.
Human and financial resources are required for this. Meanwhile, health departments across
the U.S. are already struggling with funding and staffing cuts. Maria Godoy, NPR News.
President Trump's controversial nominee to be inspector general at the Interior Department
faces an initial confirmation hearing tomorrow in the Senate, and PR's Kirk Sigler reports Dennis
Kirk is a Trump loyalist who also co-authored part of the right-wing playbook Project 2025.
Trump nominated Dennis Kirk to be inspector general at the Department of the Interior last
August. Democrats and environmentalists argue Republicans are ramming through his nomination
during the lame duck Congress. Tim Whitehouse is with Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility.
Our concern is taxpayer and park visitor money is flowing to politically connected donors and
contractors with no bidding, no transparency, and no answers to Congress. Current and newly elected
Democrats in the next Congress say they're eager to investigate how contracts like those for the
reflecting pool were no bid, and the Interior Secretary Doug Burgum's new strategic plan that
calls for using more federal public lands for data centers and selling some parcels. Kirk Sigler,
NPR News. Home builders are feeling grim as they deal with a variety of challenges. NPR's Scott
Horsley reports an index of builder confidence has dropped to its lowest level in 14 years.
The housing market has been hammered by persistently high mortgage rates. At the same time,
builders are having to contend with rising costs for materials and that immigration crackdown has
led to a shortage of construction workers. Put it all together, the National Association of Home
Builders' Confidence Index has dropped to its lowest level since 2012, when the housing market
was just beginning to recover from the Great Recession. 46 percent of builders cut prices
this month in an effort to attract scarce buyers, with an average discount of 6 percent.
Builder confidence has been slumping across the country with the lowest readings in the west and
the south. Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington. A.I. stocks led widespread losses on Wall Street
today. The S&P 500 sank 1 percent. This is NPR. Claims by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's
Likud Party that the recent Israeli election was stolen by Arab-led parties are unraveling.
Israeli authorities say they've found no evidence to support them, and now Israel's attorney general
is looking into suspicions that unsubstantiated claims of voter bribery originated with Netanyahu's
own staff. Netanyahu's chief rival, Gadi Isencon, is moving ahead with efforts to form a new
government and oust him. After NASA launched it almost 50 years ago, the Voyager 1 probe
documented the planets and eventually left the solar system. Sandin Tautin reports the spacecraft's
about to achieve another major milestone. Early Wednesday morning, Voyager 1 will reach a distance
of exactly one light day away from Earth. A light day is how far light travels in just 24 hours.
It's about 16 billion miles. NASA scientist Linda Spilker worked on the project when it launched.
She says over the last five decades, Voyager completely upended what we knew about space.
For me, it's not a surprise anymore that many of the things that Voyager is finding don't necessarily
agree with the models that we have. Voyager holds the record for the furthest any human-made object
has traveled in space. Wednesday morning, it'll pass that light day mile marker,
then plow forward into the unknown. For NPR News, I'm Sandin Tautin.
Pope Leo is forgiven the person who hit him in the eye with a rosary during a
Popemobile ride before his final mass in Peru. Leo brushed off the incident as merely someone
